A function declaration can be called above the line that defines it. A function assigned to a variable exists only after that line has run. If a project mixes both, you have to check how each function is written to know where it can be called.

This rule makes you pick one. By default it asks for expressions.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function formatName(user) {
  return `${user.first} ${user.last}`;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const formatName = function (user) {
  return `${user.first} ${user.last}`;
};

const initials = (user) => user.first[0] + user.last[0];
```

`export default function` is never reported, and neither is a TypeScript function that has overload signatures:

{/* good */}
```ts
export default function main() {}

function parse(input: string): string;
function parse(input: number): number;
function parse(input: string | number) {
  return input;
}
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
func-style = ["error", "declaration", { allowArrowFunctions = true }]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `"expression"` (default) | Report function declarations. |
| `"declaration"` | Report functions assigned to a variable where it is declared. |

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowArrowFunctions` | `false` | With `"declaration"`, allow arrow functions. |
| `allowTypeAnnotation` | `false` | With `"declaration"`, allow a function if its variable has a type annotation. |
| `overrides.namedExports` | not set | The style for `export function` and `export const`: `"declaration"`, `"expression"`, or `"ignore"` for either. |

### `"declaration"`

{/* bad {"options": ["declaration"], "count": 2} */}
```js
const formatName = function (user) {
  return `${user.first} ${user.last}`;
};

const initials = (user) => user.first[0] + user.last[0];
```

{/* good {"options": ["declaration"]} */}
```js
function formatName(user) {
  return `${user.first} ${user.last}`;
}
```

An arrow function that uses `this` is not reported, because `this` would mean something else in a declaration:

{/* good {"options": ["declaration"]} */}
```js
function Timer() {
  const tick = () => {
    this.seconds++;
  };
  setInterval(tick, 1000);
}
```

### `allowArrowFunctions`

{/* good {"options": ["declaration", {"allowArrowFunctions": true}]} */}
```js
const initials = (user) => user.first[0] + user.last[0];
```

### `allowTypeAnnotation`

A declaration cannot be given a function type as a whole, so this option lets such functions stay expressions:

{/* good {"options": ["declaration", {"allowTypeAnnotation": true}]} */}
```ts
type Handler = (event: Event) => void;

const onClick: Handler = (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
};
```

### `overrides.namedExports`

{/* good {"options": ["expression", {"overrides": {"namedExports": "declaration"}}]} */}
```js
export function formatName(user) {
  return user.name;
}

const trim = function (text) {
  return text.trim();
};
```

{/* bad {"options": ["expression", {"overrides": {"namedExports": "declaration"}}]} */}
```js
export const formatName = function (user) {
  return user.name;
};
```
